verdict.rationale: Meilisearch's first-party docs describe built-in typo tolerance (e.g. 'phnoe' finding 'phone') that works with no tuning, and a dedicated 'typo' ranking rule. They also document per-index configuration and a minWordSizeForTypos object for overriding the default thresholds that control when fuzzy matching applies. Missing for 10: the evidence names only minWordSizeForTypos (other tunable options such as disabling typos on specific attributes or words are not shown), and no independent or hands-on corroboration of typo tolerance.

support.subject: As a developer, searches tolerate typos and misspellings out of the box, with tunable rules for when and how fuzzy matching applies

citations.quote: Typo tolerance helps users find relevant results even when their search queries contain spelling mistakes or typos, for example, typing `phnoe` instead of `phone`.
Help users find what they want instantly, even when they misspell or only remember part of it. No tuning required.
You can override these default settings using the minWordSizeForTypos object.
You can configure the typo tolerance feature for each index
